title: Compatibility Facade for Vector-Ranker: iterator pagination, HTTP error mapping, and streaming parity
creator: Marcus Vega
description: We need a runtime-facing compatibility facade that normalizes client interactions across legacy and new vector/embedding-based ranking endpoints. The goal is to ensure parity for streaming outputs, function/tool-calling handshakes, structured response envelopes, and a single, predictable pagination + error contract so downstream SDKs and enterprise customers do not need multiple adapters. This ticket scopes the engineering deliverable: a wire-format adapter (request/response layer) and runtime integration tests that validate behavior across the three modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
acceptance_criteria: Facade accepts legacy iterator cursors and modern page tokens and returns stable, idempotent cursors for retries
Streaming rank responses expose the same prefix/continuation behavior as non-streaming endpoints and support mid-stream tool/function-calls without breaking cursor semantics
HTTP error codes are mapped to a small canonical set (400/401/403/429/500) with structured error bodies that include our standardized error_code and retry_hint fields
When fallback to a lower-capacity model happens, the response includes clear degradation metadata and a deterministic canonical substitute code for client logic
Automated e2e tests exercise: legacy client -> facade -> new ranker; new client -> new ranker; and partial stream -> function-call -> resume scenarios
Documentation and SDK adapter examples updated for Node/Python showing migration from legacy to the facade with minimal changes
No customer-facing breaking changes for existing embed-search/rerank customers during a staged rollout with canary traffic (<=5% initial)
updates: 2026-02-12: Ticket created after PM workshop; initial scope and acceptance criteria drafted. Linked research notes.

2026-02-18: Spike complete. Prototype adapter that converts legacy cursor to page token created in repo (github.com/redwood-inference/compat-adapter, branch: eng/compat-spike). Observed cornercase where streaming responses and tool-calls race on cursor materialization.

2026-02-25: Design review with Product and DX. Agreed to add explicit handshake message in stream for function-calls to mark cursor-consistent checkpoints. Action: add interstitial 'checkpoint' event in streaming protocol.
2026-03-02: PR submitted for initial adapter + unit tests (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-adapter/pull/42). Requesting eng review from @julia-martin and @emil-choi.
2026-03-07: Found incompatibility in legacy clients that assume header-based cursor lifetimes. Added mitigation plan: accept both header and body cursors for 3 release cycles.
2026-03-10: Implemented canonical error mapping table and integration tests. Blocking item: SDK release coordination window unclear (pinged SDK leads).
decisions: Use a single canonical error schema: {error_code, message, retry_hint, inner_errors} and map all upstream/legacy errors to this shape
Introduce a lightweight streaming 'CHECKPOINT' control message that marks a durable resume point for iterators and tool-call resumption
Support both legacy cursor tokens and new opaque page_tokens for 12 months; after which we will deprecate legacy cursors with warning headers
Fallback model substitution will include both model_id and a degradation_score to allow deterministic client-side routing logic
